proposed_relationship: Lipid nanoparticles can be used to deliver modified-nucleoside mRNA encoding viral surface proteins to cells in vivo, inducing an immune response.
mechanism: The use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) allows for efficient delivery of nucleic acids into the cytoplasm of cells. By incorporating modified-nucleoside mRNA, such as pseudouridine or N1-methylpseudouridine, into the LNPs, the mRNA can evade innate immune sensors (TLR7/8) and be translated into protein. If the mRNA encodes viral surface proteins, such as the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, the translated protein can be recognized by the immune system, potentially inducing a neutralizing antibody response.
constraint_released: The need for months to years of manufacturing scale-up for conventional vaccine platforms is alleviated by using LNPs and modified-nucleoside mRNA.
predicted_quantitative_outcome: 90% of vaccinated individuals will produce neutralizing antibodies within 4 weeks
